# Ryeton

> Ryeton buys independent, owner-run condo, co-op and HOA management firms (managing agents) in New York, keeps their teams and brands, and runs them for the long term. Software prepares routine work; a manager reviews, approves and stays responsible.

Ryeton was founded in 2026 in New York by Ilia Sotonin, who built and ran a residential management company serving 20,000 residents and then built management software used by 10,000 management companies, and Alexander Kostromin, who has run New York residential operator Outpost since its launch (4,000+ units over 10 years).

## For owners of management firms

- [Sell your firm, keep what you built](https://ryeton.com/): who we buy from, how a sale works, what stays the same, questions owners ask
- Firms we look for: New York City and nearby counties; co-ops, condos and HOAs (some rentals are fine); about 1,000 to 5,000 units; an owner thinking about what comes next
- How a sale works: a private first call; numbers under a mutual NDA; an indication of value; a letter of intent with price, structure, your role, your staff and timing before anything is binding; an independent accountant's review; closing usually 60 to 90 days after the letter
- Deal shapes: sell all or part of the firm; most of the price at closing and a portion as clients stay; keep a stake and stay on, or hand over at your pace
- Commitments: the team stays; boards hear about it from the owner on an agreed plan; managers decide; everything in writing; the owner chooses what comes next
- Ryeton never sells a firm on its own; it stays part of a group run for the long term
